rationale: Both follow the same validation sequence and are easy to read. A is a bit clearer and more precise. Its explicit allow-list regex for punctuation, followed by stripping non-digits, states the accepted characters directly. Its single if/elif chain on len(digits) maps one-to-one onto the error messages. B checks 'len > 10' after possibly stripping the country code and then reports 'greater than 11 digits', so the reader has to reason about the earlier mutation. B's str.isdigit() check also accepts non-ASCII digit characters such as superscripts, which A's [0-9] class rejects. A's pretty() reuses the area_code property in an f-string, which is slightly more idiomatic than B's str.format with repeated slicing. The differences are small but favour A.
